item.research_question: How can the Co-Ni balance in a VCrFeCoNi medium-entropy alloy system be tuned to induce an fcc to bcc martensitic transformation for enhancing cryogenic strength-ductility balance?
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction melting of pure elements (99.9% purity), homogenization at 1100 °C for 6 hrs, cold-rolling with 75% reduction ratio to 1.5-mm sheets, and annealing at 900 °C for 10 min followed by water-quenching
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature (25 °C) and cryogenic temperature (−196 °C) with a crosshead speed of 6.4 × 10−3 mm·s−1
key_findings: The 35Co alloy achieved a cryogenic tensile strength of 1623 MPa, which is twice its room-temperature strength.
At cryogenic temperature, the 35Co alloy exhibited 65% elongation and a yield strength of 653 MPa.
The fraction of fcc phase in the 35Co alloy decreased to 1.1% after cryogenic tensile deformation, indicating extensive fcc to bcc transformation.
The 30Co alloy showed a multiple-stage strain hardening behavior with a hardening rate reaching 3600 MPa in Stage III.
The hcp phase fraction was approximately 5% and acted primarily as a nucleation site for the bcc martensite.
Increasing Co content from 10 to 35 at.% reduced the Gibbs free energy difference (ΔGbcc-fcc) from −1300 to −5800 J·mol−1.
The 35Co alloy displayed a sigmoidal stress-strain curve at cryogenic temperatures, consisting of an easy deformation stage followed by rapid hardening.
item.mechanism: The fcc to bcc martensitic transformation generates a complex network structure with high-angle grain boundaries that refines the grain dynamically and introduces large transformation strains, creating mobile dislocations that significantly enhance strain hardening and strength-ductility balance.
item.limitations: The authors note that thermodynamic calculations using the database are not accurate below 0 °C, though 0 °C calculations are considered reasonably acceptable for stability evaluation.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the fcc to bcc transformation can be an attractive route for a new MEA design strategy to improve cryogenic strength-ductility.
quotes: The Co-Ni balance plays a leading role in phase stability and consequently tunes the cryogenic-temperature strength-ductility balance.

The resultantly formed bcc martensite favorably contributes to the transformation-induced plasticity, thereby leading to a significant enhancement in both strength and ductility as well as strain hardening.

Outstanding cryogenic-temperature tensile properties (e.g., yield strength; 653 MPa, tensile strength; 1623 MPa, elongation; 65% in the 35Co alloy) were attributed to the continuously increased strain hardening in the later deformation stages.
